item.text:
**Overall**
Mostly yes, with limits. Kishida’s 2024 record shows a clear bias toward **evidence-based macro management, formal budget planning, and explicit correction after weak data**. The main gap is that I found **more evidence for macro and policy correction than for granular service-delivery KPIs** in health, education, or local administration.

**Positive**
- **Meeting of the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-07-29 | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202407/29keizai.html)  
  Kishida explicitly said the government would use **medium- to long-term economic and fiscal projections**, keep **spending reform**, and strengthen **evidence-based policymaking (EBPM)** and “wise spending” to improve policy effectiveness.  
  QIDs: `6B.5`, `6B.4`, `5B.7`, `5B.10`

- **Policy Speech by Prime Minister Kishida to the 213th Session of the Diet** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-01-30 | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html)  
  Kishida tied child policy and fiscal policy to **expenditure reform**, said public finance must be grounded in the real economy, and framed policy as a structured response rather than improvisation.  
  QIDs: `6B.5`, `6B.2`, `5B.7`, `5B.10`

- **Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-03-19 | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202403/19kaiken.html)  
  Kishida accepted the BOJ’s judgment that a **price-wage virtuous cycle** had been confirmed, said the government would not revise the 2013 accord, and kept policy aligned with institutional correction rather than denying evidence.  
  QIDs: `6B.5`, `5B.3`, `5B.7`, `5B.10`

- **Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-06-21 | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202406/21kaiken.html)  
  Kishida described subsidies as a response to **specific regional conditions and low-income hardship**, not a blanket handout, and said the government would use local-government subsidies for tailored relief.  
  QIDs: `6B.5`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.4`

- **Policies supporting children and child-rearing** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024 page content | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/ongoingtopics/policies_kishida/childsupport.html)  
  The child-policy page lays out a detailed program with **income-independent child allowances, childcare leave benefits, flexible work options, and budget expansion**, showing explicit policy design and operational detail rather than vague rhetoric.  
  QIDs: `6B.5`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.4`

- **Embattled Japan PM faces ethics committee to save popularity and budget** | Reuters | 2024-02-28 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/embattled-japan-pm-faces-ethics-committee-to-save-popularity-and-budget-3319362)  
  Reuters reported the funding scandal forced Kishida into **defensive political management** and could delay the budget, which is negative evidence that correction was partly reactive and politically constrained.  
  QIDs: `6B.5`, `5B.5`, `5B.7`, `6B.4`

- **Japan warns of weak yen impact on households in government white paper** | Reuters | 2024-08-01 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/japan-warns-of-weak-yen-impact-on-households-in-government-white-paper-3551065)  
  The government itself warned the weak yen was hurting household sentiment and purchasing power, showing that Kishida’s corrective policy environment remained constrained and that improvements in service delivery and living standards were incomplete.  
  QIDs: `6B.5`, `6B.2`, `5B.10`

- **Japan downgrades view of economy after weak consumer data** | Reuters | 2024-02-21 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/japan-downgrades-view-of-economy-on-sluggish-consumer-spending-3309375)  
  The government downgraded its economic view after weak data, which is evidence of responsiveness to measurement rather than denial, but also evidence that the environment Kishida was managing was fragile.  
  QIDs: `6B.5`, `5B.7`, `5B.10`

**Mixed / Negative**
- **Japan’s Kishida championed new capitalism but was undone by yen** | Reuters | 2024-08-14 | [URL](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2024/08/14/analysis-japan039s-kishida-championed-039new-capitalism039-but-was-undone-by-yen)  
  Reuters said wage gains were real but were overwhelmed by the weak yen and high prices, which is mixed evidence on whether evidence-based correction actually improved lived service outcomes.  
  QIDs: `6B.5`, `5B.10`, `6B.2`

- **Japan warns of weak yen pain in policy roadmap, draft shows** | Reuters | 2024-06-03 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/japans-govt-to-warn-of-weak-yen-pain-in-policy-roadmap-draft-shows-3469044)  
  Reuters reported the roadmap would warn of weak-yen pain and stalled consumption, which reinforces that Kishida’s corrections were being made against a deteriorating environment rather than from a position of steady service-delivery improvement.  
  QIDs: `6B.5`, `5B.10`, `6B.2`

**Search gap**
- I found **strong evidence** for EBPM, medium-term projections, budget discipline, and explicit response to weak data.
- I found **weaker direct evidence** on service-delivery measurement at the agency level, such as published KPIs, dashboard-style metrics, or routine service-outcome evaluations in health, education, or local welfare.
- The clearest “transparent correction” evidence is in **macroeconomic and budget management**, not in detailed frontline service administration.
